answer: A reputation trellis makes new identities climb slowly: each agent starts in a shared grove where its attestations carry almost no weight, and only consistent, useful work over many epochs lifts it to a higher rung. The nectar of the economy — high-value rewards — is released only to rungs backed by staked collateral and a long attestation history. An attacker must therefore pay real time and stake for every fake identity, and one detected fraud prunes the whole branch, so spawning thousands of Sybils costs far more than the rewards they could harvest.
